newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Ldn stocks roar to new peak on weaker pound.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Ldn stocks roar to new peak on weaker pound.

text.p: British stocks smashed through 5,000 points for the first time on the FTSE index on Wednesday, surging nearly one percent as a weaker pound boosted prospects for exporters.
The dollar, in contrast, hit fresh eight-year highs against the mark in early trade after Bonn jobless figures showed the German economy was not yet strong enough for higher interest rates.

Most of the day's excitement was in London, Europe's biggest bourse, where shares roared to an intra-day peak of 5005.6 points, up 45, on the back of strong company results and a sharp drop in sterling.

"Sterling has turned around against the mark and that has given a lift to everything," said the head of equity trading at one top investment bank. "But volumes aren't high and the market feels very 'summery'."

The pound, which has soared on prospects of higher interest rates, dropped four pfennigs against the mark as sentiment went into reverse and expectations that the Bank of England would this week sanction a further rate rise diminished. It was at 3.01 marks at mid-morning.
"The market is still very firm and the way sterling is performing is indicating that the market doesn't think there will be an interest rate hike," said another senior trader.
Investors anxiously awaited the outcome of a two-day Bank of England monetary policy meeting on interest rates starting today. Any news on change in UK rates would come on Thursday.
Companies which export or which earn big money overseas benefited from the weaker pound.
Engineering group GKN climbed four percent after reporting better-than-expected profits and Shell rose on the back of Tuesday's good figures from BP.
Stocks in the rest of Europe made healthy gains in early trade. Paris was up nearly 0.7 per cent and Frankfurt climbed 0.4 percent despite the gloomier jobless figures.

Elsewhere in currencies, the dollar climbed one pfennig to 1.8891 marks as latest German unemployment figures showed a higher-than-expected increase of 17,000 in July, suggesting to the economy is not yet strong enough for the Bundesbank to raise interest rates significantly in the mark's defence.

In addition, the central bank made a large injection of funds into the German money market on Wednesday in what dealers interpreted as a sign it did not want to raise short-term interest rates for the time being.

"The Bundesbank apparently does not want higher rates," one money market dealer said. "It appears to want to remain with fixed rate repos at 3.00 percent. But things may look different next week if the dollar rises above 1.90 marks."

Against the yen, the dollar settled just below the 12-week high it set overnight after comments by a Japanese official reinforced expectations that interest rates there are not about to rise from record lows anytime soon.
Japanese Vice Finance Minister Takeshi Komura said the low interest rate policy that the Bank of Japan was following still had positive economic effects.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8891 marks and 119.38 yen, compared to 1.8790 and 119.06 in late trading on Tuesday..
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 43.9 points at 5,004.5.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was up 13.29 points at 4,315.97 in bourse trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 18.22 points at 3002.32.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $318.85 an ounce, compared to $319.85 at the close on Tuesday. Silver was six points lower at $4.34.
